subject: Accounting
title: CPAs Come to America
description: Learn CPAs Come to America in one minute.

hook.text: New York passed a law in 1896 creating the Certified Public Accountant designation.

buildup.text: America modeled the CPA on Britain's chartered system but added state-level licensing.

discovery.text: Candidates had to pass a rigorous exam covering auditing, law, and accounting theory.

twist.text: Each state set its own rules—creating 50 different sets of CPA requirements for decades.

climax.text: The Uniform CPA Exam eventually standardized the profession across the country.

quiz.question: When was the CPA designation first created?

details.summary: The Certified Public Accountant designation was created in the United States in 1896 when New York became the first state to pass CPA legislation, establishing American accounting as a licensed profession with legal standards.
details.whyItMatters: The CPA designation created a legally recognized standard for accounting competence in America, protecting the public and establishing the framework that governs the largest accounting profession in the world.
takeaways: New York passed the first CPA law in 1896, creating a legally recognized accounting credential
The CPA examination became a standardized test of accounting knowledge and competence
Every U.S. state eventually adopted its own CPA licensing requirements based on the New York model

faq.question: When was the CPA designation created?
faq.answer: The CPA designation was created in 1896 when New York passed the first CPA legislation in the United States. Other states followed, and by the early 20th century, CPA licensing existed nationwide with standardized examination requirements.

faq.question: What is the difference between a CPA and a regular accountant?
faq.answer: A CPA has passed a rigorous national examination, met education and experience requirements, and holds a state license. Regular accountants may do bookkeeping and financial work, but only CPAs can perform certain regulated activities like signing audit opinions.
